issues.display_title: Issue #105: The signed-in account can be removed from the upload account list
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

In the upload account list (Upload to GoThru), the account the app itself is signed in with
shows a remove (×) button, so it can be deleted from the list like any other account. It is
supposed to have no remove button at all.

How to reproduce

  1. Sign in to the app with account A
  2. Select some images and open Upload → GoThru
  3. Add New Account and sign in — with account B, or with account A again
  4. Reopen the upload panel

Account A now carries a remove button next to it.

It does not happen on a fresh sign-in; it starts once the stored sign-in has been renewed —
signing the same email in again from the upload modal is the quickest way to see it.

Goal

The account the app is signed in with should never offer a remove button in the upload account
list. The only way to sign out of it stays where it already is, in the user menu. Other accounts
added for uploading keep their remove button.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — the same code is on development and in the old Electron
app (ListAccounts.tsx:459). The list hides the button by comparing tokens, but a token is not a
stable identity: every sign-in issues a new one, and signing in from the upload modal replaces the
stored token while the app's own copy stays behind, after which the two never match again.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario H9).

issues.display_title: Issue #103: Typing a wrong path throws you out to "My Computer" with no message
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Type a folder path that doesn't exist into the path bar and press Enter (or click Apply), and
the app silently dumps you at the "My Computer" drive list. The folder you were working in is
gone from view, with no message explaining why.

The same thing happens without any typing: if a folder you have open gets renamed, moved, or
sits on a drive you unplug, the app throws you back to the drive list a few seconds later —
again with no explanation.

How to reproduce

  1. Open any folder in Preview (also happens in Edit and File Manager)
  2. Click the pencil icon in the path bar to edit the path
  3. Add some junk to the end of the path so it points nowhere, e.g. ...\panoramas\360 - Office
    → ...\panoramas\360 - Officeasdasd
  4. Press Enter, or click Apply
  5. The grid empties and you land on the "My Computer" drive list (C:, D:, …)

Goal

A wrong path should not cost you your place. Tell the user what went wrong and leave them where
they were:

  • Typing a path that doesn't exist should show a message and keep the current folder open, with
    the path still editable so the typo can be corrected.
  • A folder that disappears mid-session (renamed, moved, drive unplugged) should show a message
    and leave the listing on screen, so the drive can be reconnected or the folder renamed back
    without losing your place.
  • Whatever the fix, it should behave the same in Preview, Edit and File Manager — they share the
    same folder-watching logic.

issues.display_title: Issue #108: Videos show as broken images in the multiview grid
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

Selecting more than one file opens the multiview grid. Any video in that selection does not
render — its cell shows a broken image and the file name instead of the video.

The same videos render correctly in the browse grid on the left, so it is only the multiview
that cannot show them.

There is a second half to it: if the file being displayed happens to be a video, the whole
multiview grid disappears and the viewer switches to the single video player, even though
several files are still selected.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder holding both images and videos
  2. Select one image and two videos (ctrl+click)
  3. The multiview grid opens — the two video cells show a broken image with the file name

Then:

  1. Click the video card in the grid on the left, so the video becomes the displayed file
  2. The multiview grid disappears entirely and only the video player is left

Goal

A video in the multiview grid should show its own video frame, the way it already does in the
browse grid, and the grid should stay on screen for as long as several files are selected,
whichever one of them is currently displayed.

The card should not look clickable either. Multiview cells have no click behaviour, so the play
badge the card inherited from the browse thumbnail promises something that never happens — it
should mark the file as a video without inviting a click.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — the same markup is on development. The grid draws every
selected file as an image, and an image element cannot decode a video.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P1).

issues.display_title: Issue #104: Opening a folder from search results goes nowhere
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Search in Preview or Edit walks the whole folder tree, so the results can include folders that
sit several levels below the folder you are in. Double-clicking one of those does not open it —
a "folder not found" warning appears and the listing stays where it was.

If the folder happens to be a direct child of the current folder, it does open, but the search
box stays filled, so the search immediately runs again inside the new folder. You never see the
folder's actual contents, only search results again.

File Manager does not have this problem — only Preview and Edit.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder that has a subfolder, which itself contains another folder
  2. Open the header search, leave the recursive toggle on
  3. Type part of the name of that deepest folder
  4. Double-click it in the results
  5. A warning appears, nothing opens

Then:

  1. Search for a folder that is a direct child of the current folder
  2. Double-click it → it opens, but the search box is still filled and the listing shows search
    results instead of the folder contents

Same in Edit.

Goal

A folder in the search results should open that exact folder, wherever it lives, and the search
should end there — the listing shows the folder's normal contents, as it does in File Manager.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — same code on development. Dates back to when recursive
search was added (June); the handling was only written for File Manager, and Preview/Edit were
missed. Found while running the pre-merge test plan
(docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario H7).

🔬 Comprehensive Testing Methodologies

1. White-Box Testing (Code Review & Architecture Verification)

  • Preview & Edit Folder Navigation Handler (Browse.tsx (Preview) & Browse.tsx (Edit)): 
    const fromSearch = layout.isSearchActive;
const isExternal = files.currentDirectory === '' ? item.external : files.externalDirectory;
const path = fromSearch
  ? item.path
  : files.currentDirectory
    ? `${files.currentDirectory}/${item.name}`.replace(/\/+/g, '/')
    : item.name;

if (fromSearch) dispatch(requestSearchClose());

ipc.sendMessage({
  type: 'load-files',
  data: { path, sortObject: convertSortConfig(sortConfigs), external: isExternal, viewer: ... },
});
    • Deep Nested Path Resolution: When fromSearch is true, the handler uses item.path (which holds the full path resolved by recursive search) instead of erroneously concatenating currentDirectory + item.name. This eliminates the false "folder not found" rejection.
    • Search Bar Dismissal: Dispatches requestSearchClose() to notify the header search hook to close the search bar, reset searchKeyword = '', and bump the search generation counter, preventing the previous search from immediately re-executing in the new folder.
  • Header Search State Cleanup (useHeaderSearch.ts): 
    useEffect(() => {
  if (searchCloseRequest === 0) return;
  setOpenSearch(false);
  setSearchKeyword('');
  bumpSearchGen();
}, [searchCloseRequest, bumpSearchGen]);
    • Listens for searchCloseRequest counter increments and closes the search UI synchronously before the newly opened folder's files are loaded.

issues.display_title: Issue #110: Map can be full screen and split screen at the same time, leaving half the window blank
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

The map can end up full screen and split screen at the same time. When it does, the map draws
itself into the right half of the window while the viewer stays shrunk to the small corner
preview it uses in full screen — so the left half of the window is blank, with a thumbnail
floating in its bottom-right corner.

The only way out is the expand-exit button on that thumbnail.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder of images
  2. Expand the map to full screen
  3. Press / (the split-screen shortcut)

The window is now half blank.

Goal

Full screen and split screen are two settings of one map mode — Preferences already presents
them that way. Turning one on should turn the other off, whichever route is used: the toolbar
button, the shortcut, or Preferences.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor — the shortcut sets split screen without clearing full
screen on development too.

Separate, still open: the / shortcut does not save the mode it switches to, so a restart
returns to the previous one. The toolbar button does save it.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P2).

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

🎯 Test Objective & Scope

Verify fix for Issue #110: Map can be full screen and split screen at the same time, leaving half the window blank.
Enforce mutual exclusivity between Full Screen and Split Screen map modes across all interaction vectors:

  1. Keyboard shortcut / (useMapSplitScreenShortcut).
  2. Map toolbar buttons (MapToolbar: expand to full screen & minimize split screen).
  3. Preferences Modal (360 Viewer tab map mode settings).

issues.display_title: Issue #109: Multiview grid gets squeezed into the corner preview when the map is full screen
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

With the map expanded to full screen, the viewer shrinks to a small preview in the bottom-right
corner. Selecting more than one file there opens the multiview grid, which is then squeezed into
that corner â€” a strip of grey boxes far too small to see anything in. The column control appears
in the top-right as well, for a grid nobody can read.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder of images
  2. Expand the map to full screen
  3. Select two or three images

The corner preview turns into a row of unreadable grey cells, and a "Column" control appears at
the top right.

Goal

The multiview grid is for a viewer that has the window to itself. While the map is full screen,
selecting several files should keep showing the current file in the corner preview, exactly as
selecting one file does.

Notes

Not caused by the renderer refactor â€” the multiview decision looks only at how many files are
selected, on development too.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P2).

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

🧪 QA Tester Verification Summary & Sign-off

🎯 Test Objective & Scope

Verify fix for Issue #109: Multiview grid gets squeezed into the corner preview when the map is full screen.
Ensure that when the map is expanded to full screen (or split screen):

  1. The corner preview shows only the current active file as a single thumbnail preview (with an exit button), matching single-file behavior.
  2. The multiview grid is strictly suppressed, preventing unreadable squeezed grey boxes in the small corner container.
  3. The "Column" number input stepper is hidden from the top-right toolbar when multiview is suppressed.
  4. Active image selection updates the corner preview cleanly.
  5. Exiting map full screen or split screen seamlessly restores the multiview grid and Column stepper for multi-selected files.

🔬 Comprehensive Testing Methodologies

1. White-Box Testing (Code Review & Architecture Verification)

  • Conditional Mode Evaluation (useFlatMode.ts): 
    const flatMode = useMemo(() => {
  if (filesSelectedCount > 1 && !mapExpanded) return 'multiView';
  if (isPanorama) return 'slider';
  return 'regular';
}, [filesSelectedCount, isPanorama, mapExpanded]);
    • When mapExpanded is true (mapFullScreen || mapSplitScreen), flatMode strictly skips 'multiView' and falls back to 'slider' (for panoramas) or 'regular'.
    • This ensures that multiview is active only when the viewer has the full screen to itself.
  • Column Control Suppression (MainViewerToolbarRight.tsx):
    • NumberInput for columns is rendered under {flat && flatMode === 'multiView' ? ... : ...}.

2. Gray-Box Testing (Redux State Transition Monitoring)

  • Monitored Redux state via React Fiber during test execution:
    • State 1: filesSelectedCount: 1, mapFullScreen: false -> flatMode = 'slider'.

    • State 7: filesSelectedCount: 3, mapSplitScreen: true -> mapExpanded = true -> flatMode = 'slider' (Split screen preserves single image pane).

3. Black-Box Testing (End-to-End User Experience)

  • Verified real desktop user interactions across all 10 test states:

    • Verified corner thumbnail displays the active image clearly with functional exit button.
    • Verified Column control is not visible when map is full screen or split screen.
    • Verified exiting full screen or split screen immediately restores the multi-column layout without manual reselection.

issues.display_title: Issue #111: Map disappears in split screen as soon as more than one file is selected
issues.main_description_html:
Image Issue

What happens

In split screen, selecting two or more images makes the map disappear. The viewer takes the
whole window and shows the multiview grid instead. Deselecting back down to one file brings the
map back.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder of images
  2. Turn on split screen, so the viewer is on the left and the map on the right
  3. Select two images

The map is gone and the grid fills the window.

Goal

Split screen means the user asked to see the map. Selecting several files should keep the map
where it is and keep showing the current file in the left pane â€” the multiview grid belongs to
the viewer modes where the viewer has the window to itself.

Notes

The old behaviour was deliberate â€” the map pane hid itself whenever multiview was on â€” so this
is a change of rule rather than a defect, decided while testing: the map wins, the grid gives
way.

Not related to the renderer refactor either way; the same rule is on development.

Found while running the pre-merge test plan (docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md, scenario P2).
